title: The Man Who Didn't Press the Button #Shorts

hook.narration: In nineteen eighty-three, one man's gut feeling may have stopped a nuclear war.

visuals.prompt: A Soviet officer in a dim bunker staring at a glowing red warning console, 1983

scenes.narration: Soviet officer Stanislav Petrov was on duty when the early-warning system reported an American missile launch. Then more.

visuals.prompt: A Soviet command bunker with red lights flashing and a large illuminated map panel, officer in uniform at the desk
A glowing red alert screen showing the word ALARM in Cyrillic style, tense atmosphere

scenes.narration: Protocol said to report it up the chain. He didn't.

visuals.prompt: A hand hovering over a heavy beige Soviet telephone on a desk, shadows, hesitation

scenes.narration: It seemed strange that the US would attack with so few missiles, and he trusted that instinct.

visuals.prompt: Close-up of a tired officer's face lit red, thinking hard, sweat on his brow

visuals.sub: missiles reported, a strangely small attack

scenes.narration: He was right. The system had mistaken sunlight reflecting off clouds for missiles.

visuals.prompt: Sunlight glinting off high altitude clouds seen from a satellite's view of Earth, golden light on white cloud tops
The same officer exhaling with relief as the red lights fade to calm blue

description: In 1983, a Soviet officer judged a missile alert to be a false alarm. This is the story of Stanislav Petrov. #Shorts #History #ColdWar

thumbnail.prompt: A Soviet officer lit by red alarm lights in a dark bunker, tense, cinematic
